title: Windowed aggregation checkpointing and mismatch reconciliation for streaming metering
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Summary: We continue to see intermittent divergences between the streaming metering aggregator and the finalized billing ledger for long-running streams. Root causes include out-of-order fragment delivery, partial reconnects that reuse a session ID, and ambiguous stream termination semantics. This ticket implements a windowed checkpointing scheme plus a lightweight reconciliation job to detect and heal cumulative token mismatches before they reach billing.

Background: The current pipeline aggregates per-fragment token counts and emits final per-session totals when a terminal event arrives. In cases where a client reconnects mid-session, sends overlapping fragments, or the proxy retries frames, the aggregator occasionally double-counts or drops tokens. Existing fixes (idempotent chunk ids, fragment dedupe) reduced frequency but not all mismatch classes.

Goal: Introduce deterministic, append-only windowed checkpoints (sequence-range, cumulative-input-tokens, cumulative-output-tokens, checksum, model-hash) emitted at configurable intervals (default 30s) and persist them to the durable metering store. Add a reconciliation worker that compares the latest checkpointed cumulative totals against the finalized billing snapshot and emits corrective delta events to the billing ledger and quota subsystem. Ensure reconciliation is safe under concurrent writes and preserves idempotency.

Non-goal: This ticket does not change tokenization logic or the billing pricing model; those are covered by separate efforts.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator writes a checkpoint object for each active stream at the configured interval with fields: stream_id, seq_range_start, seq_range_end, cumulative_input_tokens, cumulative_output_tokens, model_hash, checkpoint_ts, checkpoint_checksum
Metering store persists checkpoints durably and exposes a query to retrieve the latest checkpoint for a stream within 5s of emission
Reconciliation worker runs periodically and flags streams where latest checkpoint cumulative totals differ from billing snapshot by >1 token for >2 windows
When a mismatch is detected the worker creates a corrective ledger entry that is idempotent and traceable back to checkpoint ids
End-to-end test simulating reconnects, overlapping fragments, and out-of-order frames shows no net billing divergence after reconciliation
No measurable increase in tail latency for single-request non-stream flows (<=1ms p50 added by checkpoint path)
Dashboard and alerting added for checkpoint emission rate, reconciliation hits, and corrected credit totals
implementation_notes: Checkpoint format: newline-delimited JSON in S3-like durable store; keep schema forward-compatible via version field
Use consistent hashing of model binary/manifest to detect model-switch mid-session (model_hash) so reconcilers can route to compatible price tiers
Leverage existing fragment sequence numbers: seq_range is inclusive and represents highest contiguous range acknowledged by aggregator
Checksum is an FNV64 over (stream_id, seq_range_start, seq_range_end, cumulative_input_tokens, cumulative_output_tokens, model_hash)
Writer will perform a conditional write: write checkpoint if checkpoint_ts > last_checkpoint_ts for same stream to avoid regressions
Reconciliation worker should use optimistic compare-and-swap when applying corrective delta to billing ledger and emit an audit event with both checkpoint ids involved
Record a reconciliation provenance record (checkpoint_id, ledger_snapshot_ts, reconciled_delta, reconciler_run_id) in the metering audit topic
steps: Design: finalize checkpoint schema and produce Confluence spec (link below)
Infra: add durable namespace and IAM role for checkpoint writes (S3 bucket / KV table)
Aggregator: emit checkpoints at configurable interval and guarantee conditional write semantics
Worker: implement reconciliation job and idempotent corrective ledger writes
QA: add unit tests + chaos tests that exercise reconnects and packet reordering
Rollout: feature flag the checkpoint emission and enable reconciliation for 1% of streams, then 10%, then 100%
Post-release: run a 1-week audit comparing pre/post divergence metrics and adjust thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization/deserialization and checksum validation
Integration test: simulated client that reconnects and sends overlapping fragments; assert reconciler produces zero net divergence after correction
Load test: emit checkpoints for 50k concurrent streams with default 30s interval and measure write tail latencies and storage throughput
Fuzz test: random reorder + duplicate fragment injection for 1000 streams; assert reconciler stabilizes and idempotent ledger writes succeed
Canary: enable reconciliation on internal-staging org and verify billing invoices unchanged for a day before broader rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0: behind feature flag. Deploy aggregator checkpoint writer and reconcilers to staging. Verify checkpoint storage and dashboard metrics.
Phase 1: Canary - enable for 1% of production streams. Monitor reconciliation rate and corrected token totals. Alert if corrected_token_rate > 0.5% of token volume.
Phase 2: Ramp - enable for 10% and run 48h stability window. Validate billing parity with control group.
Phase 3: Full - enable for all streams, disable feature-flag-based canary. Maintain intensified monitoring for 7 days.
Rollback: reconciliation is reversible by publishing an explicit negative corrective delta if a bug is found; immediate rollback also possible by disabling worker and preventing new checkpoint writes
